title: Keepr: Go backup service implementation
description:
Build a Go backup service with YAML config, built-in scheduler, and web UI for monitoring.

**Architecture:** Single binary daemon using rsync for backups. In-memory state with SSE for live log streaming. Cron-based scheduler replaces external cron jobs.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.25+, gopkg.in/yaml.v3, github.com/robfig/cron/v3, github.com/spf13/cobra, standard library for HTTP/exec/embed.

**Implementation phases:**
1. Tasks 1-5: Project setup and config loading
2. Tasks 6-7: State management with log buffer
3. Tasks 8-12: Backup runner (rsync, hooks, cleanup)
4. Task 13: Scheduler
5. Tasks 14-16: Web UI
6. Tasks 17-19: CLI commands
7. Tasks 20-22: Config example and testing

See docs/plans/2026-01-25-backup-manager-implementation.md for full details.

title: Fix duplicate logs in web interface
description:
## Goal
Prevent logs from appearing twice when viewing the logs page by synchronizing the initial log count between server-side rendering and SSE streaming.

## Architecture
Pass the initial log count from the client to the SSE endpoint via query parameter. The SSE handler will use this count as its starting position instead of 0, ensuring only NEW logs are streamed after page load.

## Tech Stack
Go (backend), JavaScript (frontend), SSE (Server-Sent Events)

## Root Cause
The duplication occurs because:
1. Server-side template renders all existing logs when `/logs/{name}` loads
2. SSE endpoint `/api/logs/{name}/stream` starts with `lastCount = 0`
3. SSE immediately sends ALL logs again, duplicating everything

## Solution
Pass `?from=N` query parameter to SSE endpoint where N = number of logs already rendered.

# Replace Dashboard Meta Refresh with AJAX Polling

**Goal:** Eliminate full-page refreshes on the dashboard by replacing the meta refresh tag with JavaScript-based AJAX polling that updates the DOM selectively.

**Architecture:** Add a new JSON API endpoint `/api/dashboard` that returns server status data. The dashboard JavaScript will poll this endpoint every 5 seconds and update only the changed DOM elements, preserving user state (scroll position, theme preference during toggle, etc.).

**Tech Stack:** Go (backend API), Vanilla JavaScript (frontend polling/DOM updates)

title: Create GitHub Actions CI workflow
description:
## Files
- Create: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Step 1: Create workflow file

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.25"

      - name: Build
        run: make build

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.25"

      - name: Test
        run: make test

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.25"

      - name: Run golangci-lint
        uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v6
        with:
          version: latest
```

## Step 2: Verify workflow syntax is valid

Run: `cat .github/workflows/ci.yml | head -20`
Expected: YAML file exists with correct structure

## Step 3: Commit

```bash
git add .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "ci: add GitHub Actions workflow for build, test, lint"
```

title: Implement copy button JavaScript functionality
Manual testing of copy button feature
description:
Test the copy button functionality manually.

**Test Plan:**

**Step 1: Start the web server**
```bash
go run . web --port 8080
```

**Step 2: Open logs page**
Navigate to `http://localhost:8080/logs/<server-name>` in browser

**Step 3: Test copy functionality**
- [ ] Click the copy button
- [ ] Verify button changes to "✓ Copied!" with green background
- [ ] Verify button returns to "📋 Copy" after 2 seconds
- [ ] Paste into text editor and verify all log lines are present

**Step 4: Test in dark mode**
- [ ] Toggle to dark mode
- [ ] Verify copy button styling looks correct in dark mode
- [ ] Verify copy still works in dark mode

**Step 5: Test edge cases**
- [ ] Test with empty logs (should copy empty string)
- [ ] Test with many log lines (should copy all)
- [ ] Test hover and active states

**Expected Results:**
- Copy button visible in header between theme toggle and connection status
- Button has hover effect (darker background)
- Button has active effect (slight scale down)
- Successful copy shows green "✓ Copied!" for 2 seconds
- All log lines copied with newlines between them
